subject: DPA: Geofence erasure and archival handoff — clarifications requested
messages:
From: Soren Lund <soren.lund@nordiqbank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Questions on geofence erasure handoff and archival scope

Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal is reviewing the DPA and has two specific asks we want to clarify before moving to signature:

1) Geofence erasure trigger: we need the clause to confirm whether on-demand erasure from a region triggers coordinated archival deletion across backup tiers, or whether backups are retained for 30 days for recovery and then purged. Our regulator expects an explicit timeline.

2) Hand-off to customer-owned archival: if Redwood provides an export of data for our archive, we want language that confirms Redwood will not retain copy once transfer is confirmed — including for backups or replicated snapshots.

I'm attaching the redline they started (NordiQ_DPA_redline_v2.docx) — legal flagged two paragraphs (see Section 5.b and Section 7.c). Can you confirm Redwood's operational behavior and whether we can accept minor language edits (we prefer concrete timelines vs. fuzzy "reasonable efforts").

Soren
NordiQBank — Head of Cloud Compliance

Subject: Re: Questions on geofence erasure handoff and archival scope

Soren —

Appreciate the clear call-outs. High level answers up front:
- Geofence erasure will remove active copies within the geofenced region within our standard erase window (we can commit to 48 hours for active replicas). Backups and snapshots are handled separately: we retain backups for a configurable backup TTL; the default for Hosted customers is 30 days unless the contract pins a shorter window.
- For exports/hand-off: Redwood can support a certified export and we can commit to a documented receipt-confirmation workflow. Once you confirm successful import, Redwood will schedule deletion of any remaining exported copies and will mark associated backups for purge in the next backup cycle.

That said, our legal team prefers to avoid absolute instantaneous deletion language for offsite backups and snapshots; operational constraints apply. I'm looping in Karthik (product/legal touchpoint) and Kimberly (privacy/legal) to propose a concrete phrasing that satisfies your regulator while remaining operationally accurate.

Proposed next step: Kimberly/Karthik to suggest 2 short sentence options we can propose as a DPA addendum — one conservative (30-day backup purge) and one accelerated (10-day backup purge with a certified export handshake). If either is acceptable to you we'll prepare a narrow addendum rather than changing the base DPA.

Best,
Marissa

Soren, Marissa —

Thanks for the clear ask. I reviewed NordiQ's redline PDF and produced two editable clauses below you can use in the DPA or as a short Binding Addendum. Pick whichever aligns with your regulator's expectation:

Option A (Conservative)
"Upon Customer request for geofence erasure, Redwood will remove all active copies within the specified geofence within 48 hours. Backups and immutable snapshots will be purged no later than thirty (30) calendar days following the erasure request, subject to any legal hold or regulatory obligations. Redwood will provide a certificate of deletion upon completion of the purge."

Option B (Accelerated, with handshake)
"Upon Customer request for geofence erasure, Redwood will remove all active copies within the specified geofence within forty-eight (48) hours. If Customer elects to receive a certified data export, Redwood will transfer exported data and await Customer's signed confirmation of successful import ("Receipt Confirmation") within ten (10) calendar days. Upon Receipt Confirmation, Redwood will schedule deletion of exported copies and will mark related backups and snapshots for purge in the next backup cycle (not to exceed ten (10) calendar days), except as required to comply with legal holds. Redwood will provide a certificate of deletion and a short audit log of the purge activity."

Notes: both options include carve-outs for legal holds/regulatory retention and we explicitly reference certificates/audit logs to help with evidence production. Karthik — any operational caveats to call out (e.g., cross-region replication delays, snapshot immutability cycles)?

—Kimberly
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Soren Lund <soren.lund@nordiqbank.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Nov 2027 13:44:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Questions on geofence erasure handoff and archival scope

All —

Operational clarifications to fold into the addendum if you pick Option B (accelerated):
- Exports are delivered over an encrypted transfer and staged to a transient export bucket for a maximum of 72 hours before deletion if Receipt Confirmation is not received. That window is to avoid failed-transfer edge cases.
- Snapshot immutability: some backup tiers (customer-configured immutable snapshots) obey the configured immutability window; we can only purge after that window expires unless Customer authorizes a snapshot-wipe in writing.
- Cross-region replication: if data is replicated to a secondary region for DR, erasure will trigger deletion in the primary geofence; deletion in secondary regions will follow the same timeline but may be subject to regional transfer confirmation.

Suggested language tweak for Option B to capture staging: add a clause "Export staging period: exported data will be staged for up to seventy-two (72) hours pending Receipt Confirmation; if no confirmation is received, Redwood will securely delete the staged export unless Customer requests an extension in writing."

I'll prepare one combined redline incorporating these points and send back before EOD — Marissa, can you confirm NordiQ's regulator preference (certificate + 10-day accelerated path vs 30-day conservative)?

—Karthik
Director, Product (Privacy & Compliance), Redwood Inference

Marissa / Kimberly / Karthik —

Thanks for the speedy follow-up and the two options. Our regulator has signalled a preference for concrete deadlines and auditable proof, so Option B + the staging clause looks promising. Two small asks before we lock:

1) Could Redwood extend the staging window to 120 hours (5 days) instead of 72 to give our ops time to validate import during a weekend? We will confirm Receipt within the 120-hour window.
2) Please add a short example audit log snippet to the certificate: timestamp, operation (export/delete), operator id, region, and Redaction status. This helps our compliance team match evidence to the regulator's checklist.

If you can accept those two tweaks we're prepared to sign the addendum and finalize. Appreciate the practical options — that helped move internal stakeholders.

Soren
